checked_claims.claim: FreeType repeated calls inherently leak through cycles
checked_claims.reason: Destructor releases face/bytes; Python font and bytes references do not establish a back-reference cycle. Leak test exercises repeated drawing with one font, not progressive font construction proof.

material_errors: Destructor releases face/bytes; Python font and bytes references do not establish a back-reference cycle. Leak test exercises repeated drawing with one font, not progressive font construction proof.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The premise is not established. FreeTypeFont holds its C font and optionally bytes (src/PIL/ImageFont.py:198-216), while font_dealloc releases FT_Face and allocated font bytes (src/_imagingft.c:1214-1221). These references alone do not form a cycle. The leak regression test repeatedly draws using one font and a memory limit (Tests/test_font_leaks.py:6-23); it is not evidence that current repeated ImageFont operations necessarily leak. Distinguish retained live font objects, allocator behavior, and an actual unreleased allocation using a measured reproduction before assigning a cause.

checked_claims.reason: Compatibility override is explicit, but limited raw native reader is not complete FITS implementation and override is not automatically temporary.

tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: At this pin, FitsImagePlugin provides a built-in reader using FITS headers and a raw tile (src/PIL/FitsImagePlugin.py:26-63). FitsStubImagePlugin retains register_handler for existing external handlers: it emits a deprecation warning and overrides the FITS open registration for backward compatibility (src/PIL/FitsStubImagePlugin.py:18-43). The stub obtains size/mode through the native reader, then invokes the handler (src/PIL/FitsStubImagePlugin.py:51-66). This is a transition path, not two automatically alternating loaders or a claim of complete FITS coverage.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: ImageFile subclasses implement format identification/parsing and configure image loading, while StubImageFile explicitly identifies a format and relies on external code to load it (src/PIL/ImageFile.py:315-335). BUFR demonstrates application-specific handler registration and delegation (src/PIL/BufrStubImagePlugin.py:17-24,40-55). This lets specialized handlers integrate with Pillow's image interface without implementing all format processing in that stub. Full plugin implementations do not universally guarantee zero dependencies or optimal performance; those claims do not follow from this architecture.

checked_claims.claim: Array export avoids copying and cannot be unified efficiently
checked_claims.reason: Export explicitly materializes bytes and calls np.array; performance intent and impossibility of unified protocol are unsupported.

material_errors: Export explicitly materializes bytes and calls np.array; performance intent and impossibility of unified protocol are unsupported.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The two directions have different entry points. Image.__array__ builds shape/type metadata, materializes image bytes (expanding mode 1), and returns np.array over an array-interface wrapper (src/PIL/Image.py:665-685). This is not zero-copy exposure of Pillow's internal storage. fromarray inspects a foreign __array_interface__, selects mode/rawmode, validates dimensionality, converts strided inputs to bytes, and calls frombuffer (src/PIL/Image.py:2890-2921). Their asymmetry reflects exporting Pillow data versus interpreting foreign array metadata, without proving that a unified API is impossible or less efficient.
